corrections.form_value: No abstract or full text reachable without credentials (OpenAlex, Crossref, and Semantic Scholar return no abstract; ScienceDirect returns 403; Semantic Scholar marks access CLOSED). The title points to a firm-level study of generative AI and innovation quantity versus quality, with no sign of people randomly assigned to AI on a creative task, so core is no. It is not placed in 'observational' because no record confirms a novelty, originality, similarity, or diversity outcome; both triage screeners guessed context_observational from the title alone. Reclassify if the full text shows a novelty or originality measure of innovation output.
corrections.source_says: Remove the conclusion "so core is no" and retain eligibility.core="unclear". The metadata do not establish that any eligibility criterion fails; the reason also contradicts the form's audited core value and its three unclear criteria.

confirmed: The title and the authors Yangyang Luo, Yuqing Hou, Qiaochu Li and Mingyue Wang match Crossref and OpenAlex. Crossref identifies Technology in Society, volume 88, article 103488, September 2026 (https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1016/j.techsoc.2026.103488, message.title, author, container-title, volume, article-number and published-print; https://api.openalex.org/works/https://doi.org/10.1016/j.techsoc.2026.103488, title and authorships).

The source.version correctly limits the original screening to metadata: Crossref has no abstract field, OpenAlex has abstract_inverted_index=null and Semantic Scholar has abstract=null. No abstract, full text, PDF, markdown conversion or appendix was read in this check (retrieval.json, c093.status=not_obtained; the three DOI API records cited above).

The additional publisher source also contains metadata only: the publicly accessible Elsevier XML response has coredata but no abstract or article body, despite its full-text-retrieval-response wrapper (https://api.elsevier.com/content/article/PII:S0160791X26002770?httpAccept=text/xml, entire response).

Independent access checks returned no Europe PMC DOI match, a forbidden ScienceDirect article page, and an arXiv API rate-limit error; these sources supplied no study evidence (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=DOI%3A10.1016/j.techsoc.2026.103488&format=json&resultType=core, hitCount=0; https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0160791X26002770, HTTP 403; https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=ti%3A%22Generative%20artificial%20intelligence%20and%20corporate%20innovation%22&start=0&max_results=10, HTTP 429).

The provisional design_class=other, eligibility.core=unclear and three unclear criteria appropriately reflect the missing study evidence. context_class=none is only an unclassified placeholder: an observational creativity or diversity outcome cannot be confirmed from the title (Crossref message.title; OpenAlex abstract_inverted_index=null; Semantic Scholar abstract=null).

The null randomized and analyzed participant counts are appropriate: no accessible source reports people, firms, outputs, exclusions or arm sizes. Whether fewer than 50 people were analyzed is unknown, and no randomized study of people receiving AI assistance was verified (the metadata-only DOI records cited above).

There are no outcome reported strings, effect estimates, confidence intervals or synthesis estimates to verify. The one_line_finding describes the title's research question without asserting a measured result; no quantitative finding can be confirmed (forms/c093.json, studies[0].outcomes, synthesis and one_line_finding; Crossref message.title).
summary: The form makes unsupported claims about a between-person design, a mixed population and no company involvement, and its eligibility explanation still says core is no. Only metadata were accessible, so eligibility remains unclear and has_randomized_people_study=false means no randomized study was verified, not that its absence was established.
